item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is preferable because it keeps the retry fix localized to FilesService, shares request/option/decoding logic, and tests a real streamed os.File upload. It still violates parts of the frozen contract, but A’s SDK-wide retry alteration and duplicated Add machinery are riskier.","reasons":["B reuses multipartbody.NewFile and verifies the multipart field, filename, content, and replay after a 429 using an actual open file.","B centralizes option handling, request construction, and response decoding in one private add implementation; A duplicates the existing Add implementation inside Upload.","A changes RawClient retry and body-closing behavior for every SDK request, including Files.Update, despite the contract explicitly excluding unrelated retry refactoring.","A’s GetBody implementation reuses and seeks the same underlying reader rather than producing an independent body, broadening behavioral and concurrency risk beyond file uploads."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, violating the contract and creating maintenance drift.","The global enableBodyReplay change alters ownership and closing semantics for seekable bodies throughout the SDK.","The Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than demonstrating streamed source content, and there is no source-reader failure test."],"risks_b":["Add now eagerly buffers every custom body, changing the lower-level API’s streaming, memory, timing, Content-Length, and error semantics contrary to the requirement to preserve its behavior.","Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, so it misses the contract’s literal routing requirement.","Tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures."]}
